skill.name: lipsync
skill.description: Use RunComfy models to sync a video face or portrait with a voice track. Includes routes for Sync Labs, OmniHuman, Kling, and Creatify.
skill.summary: Route lip-sync requests to the right RunComfy model with consent-aware CLI guidance.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: Static command, network, filesystem, and blocker findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, documentation links, placeholder URLs, and secure token-storage documentation. I found no prompt injection or hidden exfiltration in SKILL.md. The remaining risk is dual-use synthetic media without built-in consent enforcement.

remediation.issue: Consent is documented but not enforced before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory pre-run confirmation that the target face and voice are authorized, and refuse public figures or sexual, defamatory uses.

remediation.issue: Media URLs are sent to an external RunComfy service.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before upload, require user-provided URLs only, and describe what data leaves the local environment.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on a local external CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Keep allowed tools scoped to Bash(runcomfy *) and avoid adding package-manager commands to the executable tool scope.

semantic_findings.title: Dual-Use Synthetic Media Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill can drive a real person's mouth from a separate audio track and states that it does not gate inputs. This can enable impersonation or non-consensual synthetic media if an operator ignores consent checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly describes dual-use lipsync, lack of built-in gating, and consent requirements for both target face and voice. The finding concerns abuse potential rather than hidden code execution.

content.value_statement: Lip-sync work can require choosing between many video, avatar, and script-driven models. This skill selects a RunComfy route and prepares a CLI run for consent-based video dubbing.
actual_capabilities: Selects a RunComfy lip-sync route based on video, portrait, audio, or script inputs.
Prepares RunComfy CLI runs for Sync Labs, OmniHuman, Kling, Creatify, Wan, and HappyHorse routes.
Maps common inputs such as source video, portrait image, voiceover audio, and output folder.
Explains quality, budget, and route tradeoffs for dubbing and talking-head workflows.
Documents consent checks, token handling, allowed endpoints, exit codes, and troubleshooting basics.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and an authenticated RunComfy account.
Sends media URLs and job data to RunComfy rather than processing video locally.
Does not verify identity rights, voice rights, or subject consent automatically.
Works best when users provide accessible media URLs and clean voice audio.

use_cases.title: Localize Brand Videos
use_cases.description: Sync translated voiceovers to approved source videos while preserving camera, lighting, and body motion.

use_cases.title: Create Talking Presenters
use_cases.description: Turn an approved portrait and voiceover into a talking-head video for demos, training, or social clips.

use_cases.title: Prototype RunComfy Workflows
use_cases.description: Choose a model route, prepare inputs, run the CLI, and inspect errors from a repeatable command flow.

prompt_templates.title: Sync an Existing Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one video and one audio file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the lipsync skill to sync this approved source video with this approved voiceover: [video URL] and [audio URL]. Use the standard route unless Pro is needed.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Talking Presenter
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking-head video from this authorized portrait and voiceover: [image URL] and [audio URL]. Choose the best RunComfy model and explain the route.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [input type], [quality target], and [budget limit]. Compare the suitable lipsync routes, then recommend one before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Batch Dubbing
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a batch lipsync workflow for [number] approved voiceovers using this approved source video. Include naming, duration checks, retries, and consent checks.

output_examples.input: A user provides an approved training video and a clean Spanish voiceover.
output_examples.output: The skill chooses Sync Labs Pro for high-fidelity dubbing, confirms consent, prepares the RunComfy run, and saves the synced result.

output_examples.input: A creator provides an authorized portrait and a product-pitch audio file.
output_examples.output: The skill selects OmniHuman, explains portrait framing requirements, runs the job, and returns the generated talking-head video location.

output_examples.input: A team wants to compare cheaper and premium routes before a batch job.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes route tradeoffs, recommends a draft route for testing, and lists checks for duration, voice quality, and consent.

best_practices: Confirm written permission for both the face and voice before every run.
Use clean voice audio without music or noise for better mouth alignment.
Match audio duration to the source video before starting a production job.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for public figures or private people without consent.
Do not run batch jobs before testing one short sample for drift and quality.
Do not add broad shell access when the RunComfy command scope is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill create audio?
faq.answer: Some routes can generate speech from text, but precise dubbing works best with a provided voiceover file.

faq.question: Can it sync a still portrait?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill routes portrait and audio inputs to avatar-style models such as OmniHuman.

faq.question: Can it preserve an existing video?
faq.answer: Yes. Sync Labs and Kling audio-to-video routes preserve the source video while changing mouth movement.

faq.question: Does it run locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI, which sends job inputs to RunComfy model endpoints.

faq.question: What inputs are needed?
faq.answer: Most runs need an approved video or portrait URL, an approved audio URL, and a target output directory.

faq.question: What safety checks are required?
faq.answer: Users must confirm consent for the face, the voice, and the intended use before generation.
